audit.summary: P1?P4 Major; P5?P8 Minor. Four Major groups comprise two false extension assertions, the global inverse-regularity gap, and a core Banach model gap. No counterexample to the main differentiable-element theorem or Hopf?Rinow on G with its stated hypotheses.
limitations: Individual smooth conjugations do not supply jointly smooth extension data — Counterevidence: Does not refute differentiable vectors or strong-metric completeness; this model has complete flat right-invariant metric.

Individual smooth conjugations do not supply jointly smooth extension data — Counterevidence: This does not disprove the differentiable-element manifold theorem or the separate Hopf?Rinow result. Fixed-parameter conjugations really are smooth; the failure is the stronger joint conclusion.
Respecting the kernel does not imply descent of a local addition — Counterevidence: Standard flat addition on same extension does descend; no nonexistence of all compatible additions.

Respecting the kernel does not imply descent of a local addition — Counterevidence: The flat standard addition does descend in the same example. Therefore no claim is made that the quotient admits no compatible local addition, or that every conclusion of Theorem 5.11 is false.
False inverse formula leaves global no-loss proof incomplete — Counterevidence: Gk=G in example. Local repair by continuity of D_e L_gamma(t), IFT and global bijectivity is valid.

False inverse formula leaves global no-loss proof incomplete — Counterevidence: For this example G^k=G; it refutes the proof identity, not the theorem's full conclusion. The separate completeness argument for an already strong right-invariant metric on G is not refuted.

Invalid boundedness inference in the core Banach model construction — Counterevidence: No family of right translations violating Lemma10.3 constructed. Full jet norm includes all intermediate derivatives.

Invalid boundedness inference in the core Banach model construction — Counterevidence: A fixed-k repair route is available. It does not refute the principal theorem, and the elementary sine family is not a theorem counterexample. The original simultaneous all-k/common-neighborhood assertion and the whole Banach/ILB reconstruction have not been proved here.

Normalized jet evaluation and bundle coordinate changes — Counterevidence: The original p31 proof already lists correct unnormalized derivatives; actual 10.6 needs fixed-k polynomial bounds, not the incorrect precise constants. Corrected estimates preserve that requirement. Definition9.10 already uses full jet coordinate changes; no counterexample to intended jet bundles or main theorem is asserted.

Normalized jet evaluation and bundle coordinate changes — Counterevidence: The source on p.31 already uses the correct unnormalized derivatives, and Lemma 10.6 needs a fixed-k polynomial bound rather than that precise incorrect constant. Lemma 9.10 already uses full coordinate changes.
Bracket convention inconsistency — Counterevidence: Either global convention can be used consistently; existence statements not refuted.
Bracket convention inconsistency — Counterevidence: This is a sign-convention conflict with a direct local correction. No exhaustive curvature or global downstream sign audit is claimed.
Cocycle equivalence map reversed — Counterevidence: Reverse direction works; cohomological correspondence can retain correction.

Cocycle equivalence map reversed — Counterevidence: The isomorphism is repaired by a local sign/direction correction. This does not repair P1's failure of joint smoothness, which is an independent issue.
Flat bundle splitting is semidirect — Counterevidence: No assertion of abstract group nonisomorphism beyond distinguished extension; homomorphic splitting itself valid.

Flat bundle splitting is semidirect — Counterevidence: No abstract nonisomorphism claim about all presentations of the total group is made. The existence of a splitting and its semidirect-product interpretation are retained.
